propositions: Pandoc 3.6.1 corrupts markdown-to-jira conversion by escaping code-span arrows, deleting HTML comments, and eroding table structure; a two-phase lexer with segmentation and post-render code-preservation check mitigates without enumerating pandoc quirks

A pure stateless renderer must classify units as safe (pass through), locked (phase-1 fenced/commented/indented), table, HTML tag, regex-dangerous prose, or pandoc-convertible, rendering only safe units and preserving exact bytes for all others

The 178-fixture corpus (29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose) must stabilize under five-pass re-rendering with unambiguous wiki markers (monospace, links, color) separate from ambiguous ones (bold, italic) to prevent oscillation

Inline-Jira scanner must recognize unambiguous forms and settle ambiguous bold/italic only in units containing no CommonMark-only markers, preventing re-parse cycles when prose contains rendered bullets

Module must fall back to identity with content-free wiki_render_fallback logging (pandoc_absent, conversion_failure, preservation_failure reasons) when pandoc is absent or conversion fails verification

Corpus ratios must measure rendered-body ≥0.90 and rendered-character ≥0.95 with non-vacuous changed-unit verification; pypandoc-binary==1.15 (pandoc 3.6.1) must be pinned and hard-tested on Linux/macOS with fallback for absent platforms
